messages:
maria: Hey @sam @leo — just got a ticket from Sales (account: VertexHealth) asking for a temporary bypass of the admission-control penalty that's throttling their trial fleet in eu-west-1. They hit sustained queueing and got penalized. Can we review?

sam: What penalty are they hitting? Penalty = the backpressure score 3 => soft block + rate-halve?

maria: The support logs show repeated 'admission_control: penalty_applied=3' and spike in queued requests. Ticket says demo started at 09:10 UTC and degraded around 09:17.

leo: Can you paste the short log snippet?

maria: Sure — paste from autoscaler/logs: ```
[2026-03-16T09:17:12Z] admission_control: pool=eu-west-1-gpu-pool-3 queued=237 in_flight=98 penalty=3 reason=pool_saturation
[2026-03-16T09:17:42Z] routing: enqueue_delay_ms=240 penalty_applied=true fallback=smaller-model
[2026-03-16T09:18:05Z] evictor: reclaim_attempts=2 reclaimed=0
```

anjali: Looks like their requests were large seq_len=2048 chat+tool-calls. The pool saw a transient spike when a few demo jobs ran concurrently. Autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough — provisioning lag for the VM-attach path was ~40s.

devon: Sales asked for a soft bypass (no permanent quota change) for the next 2 hours while infra finishes preprovisioning for their upcoming demos. They want token-unthrottled throughput.

sam: Operationally the penalty-bypass flow exists: a temporary override tied to account id, region, and duration. We need SRE approval if it changes fairness smoothing. @leo — can you confirm impact on fair-share?

leo: If we bypass penalty for a customer we risk impacting other tenants in that shared pool. But we can limit it: grant bypass with enforced max-concurrency=20 and route to reserved burst capacity if available. That keeps fair-share smoothing intact.

maria: Customer info: VertexHealth, account_id=acct-0x7e4, trial tier, projected demo traffic 2k tokens/min peak. They asked urgently.

anjali: Quick check on reserved burst: eu-west-1 has 2 spare nodes that are not pinned to a customer, but attaching them will take ~30s and cost run-hours. We can also spin up dedicated ephemeral nodes using the burst budget.

devon: Sales is OK with cost — they'll eat burst charges — but they want minimal impact on demo quality.

sam: Proposal: grant a temporary bypass for acct-0x7e4 for 2 hours, limit to max_concurrency=20, route to burst nodes first, enable prefix cache bypass=false (no change), and set automatic revoke at expiry. Also notify other tenants via a short message in eng-sre. Anyone object?

leo: +1 if we enforce max_concurrency and monitor queue length. Set an alert: queue > 150 => rollback bypass.

maria: I'll open the override request in the internal portal and tag @eng-sre. Setting TTL=2h and recovery watch.

ops-bot: action_taken: override_granted account=acct-0x7e4 region=eu-west-1 duration=7200s limit=max_concurrency:20 routed_to=burst_nodes initiated_by=maria

sam: Thanks — keep an eye on latency SLO for that pool and post summary when it's done.

maria: Will do. Also adding a short follow-up to infra runbook about provisioning lag for VM-attach path — we should consider prewarming in high-demo windows. :memo:

devon: FYI Sales asked to keep this quiet until demo starts. No public announcement.

leo: Noted. Logging the incident for post-demo capacity planning.

maria: Closing thread after the 2h TTL. If anything flares up, ping this channel. :thumbsup:
